subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Data Interpretation — Table and Bar Chart Based Questions (W11 B2)

questions.stem:
Study the table and answer Q1–Q5:

Production of Wheat (in lakh tonnes) by 5 states over 4 years:

State | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022
------|------|------|------|------
  P   |  12  |  15  |  18  |  21
  Q   |  10  |  12  |  14  |  16
  R   |   8  |  10  |  12  |  14
  S   |  20  |  22  |  24  |  26
  T   |   5  |   7  |   9  |  11

What is the total wheat production by all 5 states in 2021?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 2021 column total = P+Q+R+S+T = 18+14+12+24+9 = 77 lakh tonnes. Verify: 18+14=32; 32+12=44; 44+24=68; 68+9=77 ✓. Trap: 75 = misreads one state; 79 = adds 2 extra; 81 = uses 2022 column for one state.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same table from Q1]

Which state showed the highest total production over all four years combined?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Totals: P=12+15+18+21=66; Q=10+12+14+16=52; R=8+10+12+14=44; S=20+22+24+26=92; T=5+7+9+11=32. State S has the highest total of 92 lakh tonnes. Trap: P = second-highest at 66 but still below S's 92.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same table from Q1]

The percentage increase in State P's production from 2019 to 2022 is:
questions.explanation: C is correct. State P: 2019=12, 2022=21. Increase = 21−12 = 9. % increase = (9/12)×100 = 75%. Trap: 70% = 9/13×100 (wrong base); 80% = overestimates by using 12+12/15 ratio incorrectly.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same table from Q1]

In 2022, what is the ratio of production of State T to that of State P?
questions.explanation: A is correct. State T in 2022 = 11 lakh tonnes. State P in 2022 = 21 lakh tonnes. Ratio T:P = 11:21 (already in simplest form — HCF(11,21)=1). Trap: 21:11 = P:T, the ratio reversed; 1:2 = approximate (11:21 ≈ 0.52, not 0.5); 3:7 = 3/7 ≈ 0.43, not equal to 11/21 ≈ 0.52.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same table from Q1]

The average annual production of State R (2019–2022) is:
questions.explanation: B is correct. State R: 8+10+12+14 = 44 over 4 years. Average = 44/4 = 11 lakh tonnes. Trap: 10 = average of first two years only; 12 = 2021 value mistaken for average.

questions.stem:
Study the bar chart data and answer Q6–Q10:

Number of employees in 5 departments of a company:

HR: 40  |  Finance: 60  |  IT: 120  |  Marketing: 80  |  Operations: 100

Total employees in the company:
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total = 40+60+120+80+100 = 400. Verify: 40+60=100; 100+120=220; 220+80=300; 300+100=400 ✓. Trap: 380 = misses one department; 420 = adds extra 20 somewhere.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same bar chart data from Q6]

The IT department has what percentage of the total employees?
questions.explanation: C is correct. IT = 120 out of 400 total. Percentage = (120/400)×100 = 30%. Trap: 25% = 100/400 (Operations proportion); 28% = wrong calculation.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same bar chart data from Q6]

If the company hires 50 more employees, all in the Finance department, what is the new percentage share of Finance?
questions.explanation: B is correct. New Finance = 60+50 = 110. New total = 400+50 = 450. New % = (110/450)×100 = 11000/450 = 24.44% ≈ 24%. Trap: 25% = 110/440 (wrong new total — adds 40 not 50); 22% = 110/500 (wrong denominator).

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same bar chart data from Q6]

The ratio of employees in Marketing to HR is:
questions.explanation: A is correct. Marketing = 80, HR = 40. Ratio = 80:40 = 2:1. Trap: 3:1 = misreads Marketing as 120 (IT value); 3:2 = uses wrong department values.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same bar chart data from Q6]

If 20% of IT employees are transferred to Operations, how many employees will Operations have?
questions.explanation: C is correct. 20% of IT = 20% of 120 = 24 employees transferred. Operations (new) = 100+24 = 124. Trap: 120 = 100+20 (takes 20 instead of 20% of 120 = 24); 112 = 100+12 (takes 10% instead of 20%).
